content.overview: Section 447 punishes fraud, defined to include any act, omission, concealment or abuse of position committed with intent to deceive, to gain undue advantage, or to injure the interests of the company, its shareholders, creditors or any other person.
content.glance: Section 447 punishes fraud, defined to include any act, omission, concealment or abuse of position committed with intent to deceive, to gain undue advantage, or to injure the interests of the company, its shareholders, creditors or any other person.
content.study: The offence requires the dishonest intent element in the definition. Punishment is imprisonment for not less than six months and up to ten years, and a fine not less than the amount involved and up to three times that amount. Where the fraud involves public interest, the minimum imprisonment is three years. A smaller-fraud band, below the prescribed amount or percentage and not involving public interest, has a lower maximum. Section 447 is the destination of several deeming provisions, including false statements under s. 448 and certain deposit frauds. It is not attracted by every procedural default. Investigation may proceed through the SFIO route in Chapter XIV where ordered. Bail is restricted by s. 212 for SFIO cases.

examples.title: Concealment
examples.body: Concealing a liability in a prospectus with intent to deceive can be fraud.

examples.title: Mere delay
examples.body: A late filing without deceptive intent is a penalty default, not automatically s. 447.

distinctions: Section 447 is fraud. Section 448 deems a false statement in a return to be fraud. Section 449 is false evidence. Adjudication penalties under the Amendment Acts are civil and do not replace s. 447.

misconceptions.correction: Section 447 punishes fraud, defined to include any act, omission, concealment or abuse of position committed with intent to deceive, to gain undue advantage, or to injure the interests of the company, its shareholders, creditors or any other person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is every misstatement in a form fraud?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. The definition requires intent to deceive, to gain undue advantage, or to injure. A deeming section must be cited if one applies.
